lens: Hostile but fair peer reviewer for a specialist oncology journal, with no stake in the paper succeeding. Tests: is the contribution real or a restatement dressed as a correction; is the central claim supported at the weight stated; is any negative/null/UNKNOWN reported below its true strength; is anything overclaimed; is the paper internally consistent; is the structure serving the reader; could a referee act on it.
verdict:
The science is sound and the arithmetic is exact. I recomputed every Wilson interval and every Fisher p-value in the paper independently (0/3 upper 56.1, 0/5 upper 43.4, 0/2 upper 65.8, 7/15 24.8-69.9, 6/58 4.8-20.8, 4/15 10.9-52.0, 13/58 13.6-34.7, 5/15 15.2-58.3, 14/58 15.0-36.5, 28/154 12.9-25.0, 120/154 70.7-83.7, 5/154 1.4-7.4, 1/154 0.1-3.6; Fisher 1.0, 0.155, 0.0034, 0.7389, 0.5163) and every one matched to the printed digit. Every pooled arm reconstructs from the per-cohort strata (3+4=7/15, 1+5=6/58, 2+2=4/15, 1+12=13/58, 2+3=5/15, 6+8=14/58). The prevalence denominators reconstruct (24+57+11+62=154; 120+28+5+1=154). The sensitivity analysis that looked wrong on first read (0/3,4/19 -> 0/2,4/20) is right: 23 enrolled = 3 TAF15 + 20 non-TAF15, 22 evaluable. `emc_fusion_partner_pooling.py --check` on a clean archive of the pin exits 0, so the reproducibility claim in section 7 is true. The central claim -- candidate, not established -- is stated at or below the weight the data carry, the defeater travels with the headline everywhere the headline travels except one place, and I could not find a single treatment implication, mechanism overclaim or independence claim that outruns its evidence. This is better-calibrated than the review literature it is arguing with.

Two things stop it. First, one live internal contradiction, and it is in the worst possible section: section 1.3, the paper's own statement of what it adds, still sells 'a prevalence figure materially below the one the field repeats' as one of five contributions, when section 3.5 and Appendix A30 both say the pooled interval CONTAINS the ~20% the paper's own cited sources state and that 'this pooling therefore does not correct that figure'. A citing author reading 1.3 for the contribution will propagate a claim the paper retracted four sentences later. That is a blocker, not a typo, and it is the paper's own declared defect class (one-of-a-pair, A24/A31) surviving in the section a reader reaches first.

Second, and this is why 'major' rather than 'minor': the correction register has measurably outgrown the result. Appendix A is 31 rows and ~5,280 words -- 30% of a 17,300-word manuscript, and about a third LARGER than the entire Results section (~3,990 words) -- plus 16 inline 'Superseded, retained' notes threaded through the live prose and 30 attributions to internal 'blind adversarial seats'. None of that is a scientific record. Nothing here was published and then corrected; these are drafting states. No specialist oncology journal will carry a synthesis of 73 prognosis patients and 3-5 treated patients at 17,300 words, and the appendix is not a trim, it is a structural rewrite: sections 1.3, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 4.x and 5 all currently reason by pointing at correction rows. Worse, the register is actively causing the defect it exists to prevent -- A30 asserts the retraction landed 'at all four of its live sites', the fifth site is section 1.3, and the guard suite's own exclusion comment repeats the same false count because it censuses the string '~27 %' rather than the framing. Corrections tracked in an appendix are corrections not made in the text.

Strip the appendix and the seat attributions, re-derive 1.3 and 5 from section 3 rather than from the correction rows, and what is left is a tight ~5,000-word paper I would recommend accepting.
central_claim: The NR4A3 5' fusion partner is a candidate -- not established -- stratification variable in EMC: it tracks disease-specific death across the two cohorts publishing partner-stratified event counts (7/15 = 46.7% vs 6/58 = 10.3%, crude, unadjusted) but is not independent of tumour size in the one series that ran a multivariable model, while its entire published antiangiogenic-response evidence base is 3-5 TAF15 patients with zero events, which yields a direction and no magnitude.
contribution_assessment: Real, modest, and -- with one exception -- honestly sized. What is genuinely new: (1) the first pooled magnitude for the prognostic contrast, printed beside the multivariable analysis from the larger of its own two cohorts that defeats it; (2) the response contrast restated as a direction rather than a difference, with the TAF15 arm's 95% upper bound shown to sit ABOVE the comparator's point estimate in both analyses -- a distinction the reviews it cites do not make and the single most useful sentence in the paper; (3) a two-cohort null on metastasis replacing a one-cohort reversal, which is the correct direction for a correction to run. What is NOT a contribution and the paper mostly says so: the prevalence pooling. 18.2% (12.9-25.0) contains the ~20% both of its own general-prevalence sources state, so it is an interval where the literature had a point estimate, not a correction of the field -- Appendix A30 concedes exactly this and calls losing the framing 'the finding rather than a problem to write around', which is the right instinct. Section 1.3 did not get the memo. The attribution correction in 3.8 (the 'unlikely to be related to sunitinib sensitivity' hedge is 2012, not 2014) is a real and citable fix, though 'the field's most-quoted caveat' is an unsupported superlative of the same class A30 just retracted. Net: this is a synthesis whose value is calibration, not discovery, and its honest self-description on prognosis and response is its strongest asset -- which is precisely why the one place it oversells itself has to go.

blockers.where: Section 1.3 'What this synthesis adds', line 132 of the pinned file
blockers.quote: It also surfaces five things that no individual source says out loud: a response contrast whose confidence interval overlaps its own comparator; the first pooled magnitude for the prognostic contrast, immediately beside the multivariable analysis that defeats it; a metastasis claim that **neither** cohort with counts establishes, in **either** direction; a prevalence figure materially below the one the field repeats; and an attribution correction to the field's most-quoted caveat (§3.8).
blockers.why_wrong: The fourth item is a claim the paper retracts elsewhere, and section 1.3 is the section a reader and a citing author take the contribution from. Section 3.5: 'The two sources in the reference list that give a general TAF15 share -- the disease review [4] and the introduction of the model-derivation paper [12] -- both put it at about 20 %, which falls **inside** 12.9-25.0. This pooling therefore does not correct that figure: it replaces a point estimate with an interval over four independent series'. Appendix A30 is categorical: 'No source for that quoting practice was held anywhere -- and the two sources in this document's own reference list that state a general TAF15 share both give about 20 %, which lies INSIDE the pooled interval 12.9-25.0. **So the "correction of the field" framing does not survive**'. A30 lists the sites it repaired -- 'the Abstract, §3.5, the §5 claims bullet and, as an attribution, A3 above' -- four sites; §1.3 is the fifth and was missed because it states the retracted framing in words rather than with the string '~27 %', which is what the census keys on. The Abstract now reads correctly ('an interval that **contains** the ~20 % this document's own cited sources state'), so the document asserts both the claim and its retraction. Two consequences: the enumerated count 'five things' is now four; and a reader acting on §1.3 would report that this synthesis corrects the field's TAF15 prevalence downward, which the paper denies in terms. This is the paper's own one-of-a-pair defect class (A24, A31), live, in the section written to be quoted.
blockers.evidence: Pinned file line 132 vs lines 439-447 (§3.5) and Appendix row A30 (line 990). Corroborated from the guard suite at the pin: research/manuscripts/tests/test_fusion_partner_prose_matches_its_artifact.py lines 1466-1477 place '~27 %' in the declared-not-artifact-owned list with the rationale 'The claim is retracted at all four of its live sites; the string survives only inside retained `Superseded, retained` quotations and the A3/A30 appendix rows' -- an assertion about the live text that is false, held only as a comment string, and executed by nothing. Verified there is no guard on the §1.3 framing: grep of the 2,201-line suite for 'materially below' and 'field repeats' returns no hits.

p1s.quote: the two absolute statements qualified below, and equally every count and every superlative taken over the literature: §3.3's "**Two** cohorts publish EMC outcome event counts by *NR4A3* partner", §5's "the only two cohorts that publish event counts by partner" and its claims bullet's "the two cohorts publishing partner-stratified event counts", and "the largest series to test metastasis by partner *directly*" (§3.3, §5, Appendix A7).
p1s.why_wrong: Correct today -- I flattened the manuscript and confirmed each quoted phrase resolves to a real live sentence, and that Suemitsu 2025 genuinely publishes no per-partner event counts (artifact cohorts[suemitsu-2025-outcome]: 'It reports the partner distribution as explicit integers ... but publishes no per-partner event counts'), so the 'Two cohorts' superlative holds. But this is a hand-maintained roster of exact sentences and their section numbers, and nothing binds it to the document. The 2,201-line prose-vs-artifact guard suite binds numbers, identifiers, fractions, rosters and even §4.3's ordered residue tuple to the artifact; grep for 'locator', '2.3a' and 'superlative' returns nothing. Appendix A16 is the record of this exact roster having already gone stale once -- '§2.3a's locator list also named §5 and §8, neither of which contains the sentence' -- and the repair rebuilt a hand-maintained list rather than a guard. Any ordinary edit that adds an absolute claim, moves one, or rewords one silently makes §2.3a incomplete, and §2.3a is the single paragraph that bounds every exhaustiveness claim in the paper. Note also that §5's variant wording is 'the largest series to test it directly', not the phrase §2.3a quotes, so the roster is already approximate.
p1s.evidence: Pinned lines 195-217 (§2.3a); phrase counts on the flattened document; absence of any binding in research/manuscripts/tests/test_fusion_partner_prose_matches_its_artifact.py at the pin; Appendix A16.

p1s.where: Appendix A, every row that states where its correction landed -- A24, A30 and A31 in particular
p1s.quote: A30: "*"below the ≈27 % the field routinely quotes"* / *"The pooled figure is below the ≈27 % the field usually quotes"* — the Abstract, §3.5, the §5 claims bullet and, as an attribution, A3 above | four sites in **this** document
p1s.why_wrong: Each appendix row asserts, in prose, the set of live sites its correction reached, and nothing derives or checks that set. A31 already states the durable lesson -- 'a correction row is the record a later round trusts, so a row whose diff does not contain its repair converts a live defect into a closed one' -- and the repair was 'check the diff against the message before committing', which is a habit, not a guard. HR-B1 is that failure recurring in the very next round: A30 says four sites and there are five. Every future correction row inherits the same unguarded shape, and the failure mode is silent and asymmetric -- a row that overstates its reach converts a live defect into a closed one and removes it from later rounds' attention. The A3 row already delegates ('the attribution itself is retracted in A30'), so a chain of rows now depends on an unverified site count.
p1s.evidence: Appendix rows A3, A24, A30, A31 at the pin; HR-B1's demonstration; the guard suite carries the same false 'all four of its live sites' text as an inert comment at lines 1473-1474.

p2s.quote: 3. Confirmation that the sunitinib series' TAF15 patients re-enrolled on the pazopanib trial, collapsing the world's TAF15 experience to three patients.
p2s.why_wrong: Neither would kill the paper, by the paper's own text. §4.5: 'The primary analysis assumes the worst case, so the conclusion is stated at both ends and does not change between them' -- and the primary analysis IS 0/3, the three-patient world. Confirming #3 removes the secondary analysis and strengthens the caution; it falsifies nothing. #2's first half ('the pazopanib trial's non-TAF15 arm contains non-EWSR1 partners') is what §3.1 and §4.6 already assume and refuse to assert otherwise -- 'Labelling that arm "EWSR1" would be a fabrication of the trial's own composition' -- so confirming it corroborates the paper. Only #2's second half (a TAF15 patient outside the evaluable 22) is a genuine falsifier. A falsifier list is a credential; two of six items inflate it, in a paper whose whole value proposition is calibration.
p2s.evidence: Pinned §6 items 2-3 vs §3.1, §4.5, §4.6. The artifact's what_could_kill_this carries the same two items verbatim, so this is generated, not a prose slip.

p2s.quote: a 36.3-point gap, post-hoc Fisher p = 0.0034, and the first magnitude this contrast has ever had
p2s.why_wrong: 'ever' is an unbounded historical superlative sitting in the Abstract, where §2.3a's own stated principle is that 'a reader who meets only §3.1 or the Abstract should not have to find this paragraph to know the limit', and where two other absolutes were rewritten in place for exactly that reason (A16). §2.3a's blanket clause ('every superlative taken over the literature') technically covers it, but the paragraph then enumerates four superlatives by quotation and this is not among them, and the same phrase repeats unbounded in §3.3 ('This is the first magnitude the prognostic contrast has ever had'). Given no systematic search was run, the supportable form is 'the first magnitude this contrast has in the sources this synthesis examined'.
p2s.evidence: Pinned Abstract and §3.3 (both instances confirmed on the flattened text) against §2.3a's stated bound-in-place principle and Appendix A16.

p2s.quote: **Both** cohorts carrying the prognostic contrast are consultation material rather than population samples: Agaram 2014 is a tertiary sarcoma referral centre and is also the prevalence high outlier (§3.5), and Huang 2023 is a fifteen-institution FISH-confirmation series. The referral argument §3.5 makes against the prevalence estimate therefore applies with equal force to the death contrast
p2s.why_wrong: 'with equal force' is not supported by the paper's own data, and §3.5 supplies the counter-evidence: §3.5's referral argument is built on Agaram's TAF15 share being the HIGH outlier (29.2%, 'against 15.8-18.2 % elsewhere'), and the 15.8% is Huang's -- the LOWEST of the four series. A cohort showing no TAF15 enrichment is weak evidence for TAF15-selective referral bias. The error runs conservative (it overstates a limitation against the paper's own headline), so it is not dangerous, but a referee will notice the paper reasoning past its own numbers in the one direction it does not police.
p2s.evidence: Pinned §4.9 vs §3.5's per-cohort range 15.8-29.2%; artifact cohorts[huang-2023-prevalence] gives TAF15 9 of 57 assigned = 15.8%.

p2s.quote: the two disagree on sign, the pooled gap is 9.2 points with overlapping intervals, and the largest series to test it directly reports P = .728
p2s.why_wrong: P = .728 is the only statistic carrying the metastasis negative in the claims list, and it is the one Huang 2023 value with no independent corroboration: §4.7a discloses that Huang's Table 1 was transcribed by a human from the PDF because the publisher's edge 403s automation, and lists the Europe PMC abstract sentences that independently corroborate the SURVIVAL defeater (P = .004, P = .032, P = .025). P = .728 is not among them. §3.3 carries the provenance caveat for the neighbouring Discussion quotation (added by A27) and §5 carries none for this one -- the same one-of-a-pair pattern, in the same section A24 and A31 were about. Also: §4.7a's disclosure is scoped to 'Table 1 counts', while what rests on that read includes published p-values (.728, .047, 1.0, .024) and both hazard ratios.
p2s.evidence: Pinned §5 claims bullet vs §4.7a; artifact cohorts[huang-2023-outcome].published_p_values = {final_status_three_way 0.047, distant_metastasis_three_way 0.728, local_recurrence 1.0} and counts_read_from naming the human PDF read; Appendix A27.

p2s.quote: Pooling four independent molecular series — MSKCC (USA), Taiwanese institutions, Czech Republic and the Italian Sarcoma Group, whose complete author lists — 5, 20, 18 and 16 names, held unabridged in the artifact's `citations` records — intersect in nobody, on surname-plus-initials or on surname alone, and whose affiliations share no referral network
p2s.why_wrong: Two absolutes are asserted and one is measured. A26 records the author-intersection check in detail ('empty intersections on all six pairs, on surname-plus-initials and on surname alone') and says nothing about the referral-network half, which is asserted from geography alone. In a paper that insists 'an absent reading is not a reading of absence', an unmeasured absolute riding on a measured one is the shape the paper elsewhere refuses. Downgrade to what is checked: no shared authors, four countries, no evidence of a shared referral network.
p2s.evidence: Pinned §3.5 vs Appendix A26, which describes only the author check.

p2s.quote: The honest heterogeneity signal at this scale is the **range of per-cohort rates**, printed beside every pooled figure — §3.1 for the TKI-response secondary pool, §3.3 for each of the three outcome rows, §3.5 for prevalence
p2s.why_wrong: §3.5 prints four pooled figures (EWSR1 77.9%, TAF15 18.2%, TCF12 3.2%, TFG 0.6%) and one per-cohort range (TAF15, 15.8-29.2%, spread 13.4 points). The enumeration's '§3.5 for prevalence' makes it defensible on a charitable reading, but this is the third round on this exact sentence -- A22 records it as 'a universality claim about the document's own presentation, measurably false inside it', found independently by two seats -- and the repair was targeted at the two widest spreads rather than at the claim. A universality sentence that has been wrong twice should be scoped ('beside each pooled contrast this paper draws') rather than repaired again.
p2s.evidence: Pinned §2.5 vs the §3.5 table and its single range sentence; Appendix A22.

p2s.quote: an attribution correction to the field's most-quoted caveat (§3.8)
p2s.why_wrong: 'the field's most-quoted caveat' is a superlative over the literature with no source held for it, in the same sentence as HR-B1 and of exactly the class A30 retracted for prevalence ('no source for that quoting practice was ever held'). §3.8 itself makes the weaker and supportable claim -- the quote is 'usually attributed' to the 2014 series, verified against cached full texts of both. §1.3 should say that.
p2s.evidence: Pinned §1.3 line 132 vs §3.8 and Appendix A30's stated standard.

p2s.quote: ## Appendix A · Corrections and superseded statements
p2s.why_wrong: Proportion. Measured on the pinned file: 17,316 words total (wc -w); Appendix A ~5,282 words across 31 rows -- 30% of the manuscript and roughly a third larger than the entire Results section (~3,990 words) -- plus 16 inline 'Superseded, retained' notes in the live prose and 30 attributions to internal blind review seats. Nothing here was published and then corrected, so none of it is a correction of the record; it is a drafting log. It is also load-bearing in the wrong direction: §3.3, §3.4, §3.5, §4.x and §5 all now reason by pointing at appendix rows, which is how HR-B1 survived. A specialist oncology journal will not print a 17,300-word synthesis of 73 prognosis patients and 3-5 treated patients, and removing this is a rewrite of six sections rather than a cut.
p2s.evidence: Word counts computed on the pinned file by line range; 31 rows matched by regex; 16 'Superseded, retained' occurrences; 30 blind-seat attributions.

coverage_gaps: No systematic search, no registered search string, no PRISMA flow, no second reader, no protocol registration (§2.3a discloses all of this honestly). The paper never names its own design: it is a narrative/opportunistic synthesis with pre-committed pooling, and the title and abstract should say so, because 'pooled synthesis' will be read as systematic by anyone who does not reach §2.3a.

Suemitsu 2025's null ('no statistically significant correlation was detected between OS and fusion subtypes') appears only in the §3.2 exclusion table and the §1.2 overview. It is absent from §4 Limitations and from §5, the section §5 itself designates as the source of the exported endpoint sentence -- and §5's 'Not that TAF15::NR4A3 is an independent prognostic factor' bullet names only Huang and Paioli. The null cuts toward the paper's own conclusion, so the omission does not inflate the headline, but the section written to be quoted is missing a fourth series failing to establish the partner.

Grade and chemotherapy allocation are never stratified by partner anywhere, although §4.1a names both as rival explanations from Huang's own univariate list and Agaram 2014 is titled for the grade association. Acknowledged, not addressed.

The paper reports no absolute or relative risk with any adjustment, by design -- so a clinician reader gets a crude 46.7% vs 10.3% and an instruction not to use it. That is honest but leaves the reader with nothing actionable, which the paper should state as its own limitation rather than leaving implicit in §4.12.

No assessment of whether the two pooled outcome cohorts' partner-assignment assays could differentially miss TAF15 in the OUTCOME arms specifically. §4.3 makes this argument for the prevalence estimate (residues, missing-at-random) and never carries it to the death contrast, where a differential miss would bias the headline.
single_biggest_improvement: Delete Appendix A, the 16 inline 'Superseded, retained' notes and every 'caught by a blind adversarial seat' attribution from the submitted manuscript -- they are pre-publication drafting history, not corrections to a published record -- and then re-derive §1.3 and §5 from §3 rather than from the correction rows. Doing it in that order is the point: §1.3's retracted prevalence framing (HR-B1) survived precisely because the retraction was recorded in A30 instead of being carried through the live text, and A30's own claim to have reached 'all four of its live sites' was checked by nothing. A ~5,000-word paper carrying the same claims at the same weight would be stronger, more citable, and structurally incapable of the defect class that has now consumed seven rounds.
what_you_could_not_break: Arithmetic. I recomputed all 13 Wilson intervals and all 5 Fisher exact p-values from scratch; every one matches the printed value to the last digit, including the boundary cases (0/3, 0/5, 0/2) where the choice of Wilson actually matters and the paper's §2.2 justification is exactly right.

Pooled reconstruction. Every pooled arm rebuilds from the per-cohort strata in the artifact, and the prevalence denominators rebuild from the four series (24+57+11+62=154; 120+28+5+1=154; per-cohort TAF15 15.8/18.2/16.1/29.2 giving the stated 15.8-29.2 range and 13.4-point spread).

The sensitivity analysis in §3.1, which reads wrong and is right: 0/3 and 4/19 becoming 0/2 and 4/20 is consistent only if 23 were enrolled as 3 TAF15 + 20 non-TAF15 with 22 evaluable, and the stated 65.8% upper bound is exactly Wilson 0/2. I tried to break this and could not.

Reproducibility. `python3 research/manuscripts/emc_fusion_partner_pooling.py --check` on a clean git-archive of the pinned commit exits 0 with 'committed artifact reproduces from the generator's counts'. §7's claim is true as stated.

The 'Two cohorts publish event counts' superlative, which I expected to fail on Suemitsu 2025 since §3.2 excludes it for overlap rather than for missing counts. The artifact settles it: Suemitsu 'reports the partner distribution as explicit integers ... but publishes no per-partner event counts', and its endpoint is overall rather than disease-specific survival. §1.2's 'four series test the partner against outcome and only two publish per-partner event counts' is correct.

The prose-to-artifact binding. The guard suite (2,201 lines at the pin) derives §8's artifact self-census (17 citations / 13 noted / 4 with slug+status / 16 cohorts) from the committed artifact, derives §4.3's residue tuple in the order the sentence names the series, and asserts the roster counts against the cohort records. The numeric drift class that produced A19/A20 is genuinely closed. What it does not cover is prose framing -- which is where the live blocker is.

Language discipline. I searched specifically for a treatment implication, an efficacy claim, a therapeutic-window claim and a mechanism attribution, and found none. §3.7 in particular reports the one matched model pair as reading AGAINST the hypothesis, and §3.6 refuses to borrow strength from GSE28866 for the clinical claim in four numbered steps. §3.2's Sjögren row names the direction its own exclusion moves the headline. This is unusually disciplined.

The July 2011 - January 2017 accrual span in §3.1, which I suspected of being the same forbidden date-stitching A21 retracted in §4.11. It is not: both dates are treatment/accrual dates of the two TKI cohorts and both are held in the artifact.

Under-reported negatives. I looked hard for a null, an UNKNOWN or a negative stated below its true strength and found the opposite pattern throughout -- Paioli's adjustment structure is marked UNKNOWN rather than assumed, the metastasis negative is stated as unestablished in either direction rather than as a reversal, and §4.9 overstates a limitation against the paper's own headline (HR-P2-3).
could_not_check: Huang 2023 Table 1 itself. The counts, the published p-values (.047, .728, 1.0), the hazard ratios (30.60, 8.14) and the size cells rest on a human PDF read on 2026-08-08 that no automated reader can repeat; the publisher 403s automation and this sandbox's egress proxy blocks Europe PMC, NCBI and ClinicalTrials.gov. The paper discloses this (§4.7a, §8). Half the pooled prognostic evidence is therefore unverifiable by me.

Stacchiotti 2019 (Lancet Oncol) and Paioli 2021 (Ann Surg Oncol) full texts -- both genuinely closed, so the trial's partner distribution, its prior-therapy table and Paioli's adjustment structure are unverifiable here as the paper says.

Whether the ~20% figures in refs [4] and [12] are themselves independent of Agaram 2014, which matters for A30's conclusion that the pooled interval merely 'contains' the field's figure. If both reviews derive their ~20% from the same primary series, the interval is less independent of the point estimate than §3.5 implies.
The verbatim text of Stacchiotti 2020 (PMC7563993) for the metastasis attribution -- §3.3 itself flags that this rests 'by record and not by quotation', which is the correct disclosure.

By instruction, I did not read research/autonomy/, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, STRATEGY.md, the program map, any skill, or any other seat's output. My only non-manuscript reads were the pinned pooling artifact, the pinned guard test, and the pinned generator.
